learn.hook: A magic box turns 3 into 21 and 5 into 35. What is the box doing?
points: A multiplier box multiplies every number that goes in by the same hidden number.
To find the hidden multiplier, divide an output by its input: 21 ÷ 3 = 7.
Check with another pair: 5 × 7 = 35. ✔
An array is objects in equal rows. 15 dots can be 3 rows of 5 or 5 rows of 3, or 1 row of 15.
The rows and columns of every array of a number are its factors: 15 → 1, 3, 5, 15.

example.q: A box turns 4 into 36 and 6 into 54. What will it turn 9 into?

learn.reallife: Shopkeepers use a 'multiplier' too: price of 1 item × number of items.

quiz.q: A multiplier box turns 3 into 21. What is the multiplier?
The same box (× 7) gets 8. What comes out?
A box turns 4 into 36 and 6 into 54. What does it turn 9 into?
quiz.explain: The multiplier is 9 (36 ÷ 4). 9 × 9 = 81.

quiz.q: A box turns 5 into 60. What number went in if 84 came out?
15 dots are arranged in 3 equal rows. How many dots are in each row?
Which arrays can be made with 15 dots?
quiz.explain: Only rows of 1, 3, 5 or 15 fit 15 dots exactly.
quiz.mistake: Picks rows that leave dots over

quiz.q: Which number is NOT a factor of 15, using its arrays?
quiz.explain: 15 cannot be put in 2 equal rows: 1 dot is left over.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every small number is a factor

quiz.q: A box turns 7 into 49 and 2 into 14. What is the multiplier?
quiz.mistake: Uses the difference of the outputs

teach.ask: Gappu's magic box changed 6 into 42. What is the secret multiplier? How do I check it?

learn.hook: 12 = 3 × 4. So is 3 a factor of 12, or is 12 a multiple of 3? Both!
points: A factor of a number divides it exactly, with no remainder. 4 is a factor of 12.
A multiple of a number is that number times a whole number. 12 is a multiple of 4 (4 × 3).
Factor pairs multiply to the number: 12 = 1 × 12 = 2 × 6 = 3 × 4.
1 is a factor of every number.
Every number is a factor of itself and a multiple of itself.

example.q: Find all the factor pairs of 18.

learn.reallife: Packing sweets in equal boxes uses factors: 24 sweets fit in boxes of 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12 or 24.

games.title: Factor or multiple?
items: 5 is a factor of 35.
35 ÷ 5 = 7 exactly.
35 is a multiple of 5.
1 is a factor of every number.
Every number ÷ 1 has no remainder.
8 is a factor of 20.
20 ÷ 8 leaves 4.
Every number is a multiple of itself.
Any number × 1 is itself.

quiz.q: Which number is a factor of 18?
quiz.explain: 18 ÷ 6 = 3 with nothing left over.
quiz.mistake: Picks a multiple instead of a factor

quiz.q: Which is a multiple of 7?
quiz.mistake: Picks a number with a 7 in it

quiz.q: Which list shows all the factor pairs of 12?
quiz.explain: Every pair multiplies to 12, and none is missing.

quiz.q: How many factor pairs does 20 have?
quiz.explain: 1 × 20, 2 × 10, 4 × 5: three pairs.

quiz.q: Which number is a factor of every number?
quiz.explain: Any number divided by 1 leaves no remainder.

quiz.q: Which is true about the number 9?
options: 9 is both a factor and a multiple of 9
quiz.explain: 9 ÷ 9 = 1, and 9 × 1 = 9. So it is both.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a number cannot be its own factor

quiz.q: 4 × 6 = 24. Which statement is true?
options: 6 is a factor of 24 and 24 is a multiple of 6
quiz.explain: The smaller numbers that multiply to 24 are its factors; 24 is their multiple.

quiz.q: What is the missing factor? 36 = 4 × ?

teach.ask: Gappu thinks 5 is a multiple of 20. Is he right? Can you explain factors and multiples?
teach.praise: Oh! 5 is a factor of 20, and 20 is a multiple of 5!
teach.nudge: Which one divides the other exactly?

learn.hook: 13 children can stand in only one kind of rectangle — a single line! Why is 13 so special?
points: Make every rectangle (array) you can with a number of objects. The rows and columns give all its factors.
12 makes 1 × 12, 2 × 6 and 3 × 4 arrays, so its factors are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12.
Some numbers make only one array: a single row. 13 = 1 × 13 only.
A number whose only factors are 1 and itself is a prime number: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 37 …
1 is not prime, because it has only one factor.

example.q: Make all the arrays for 16 and list its factors.

learn.reallife: Prime numbers keep bank cards and online messages safe — very large primes are used in secret codes!

quiz.q: How many different arrays (rectangles) can 12 objects make? (2 × 6 and 6 × 2 count as one.)
Using arrays, which list shows all the factors of 18?
Which number can only be arranged in a single row?
quiz.explain: 13 has only 1 and 13 as factors.
quiz.mistake: Thinks odd numbers are always prime

quiz.q: Which of these is a prime number?
quiz.explain: 37 has only the factors 1 and 37. 39 = 3 × 13, 35 = 5 × 7, 33 = 3 × 11.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every number ending in 3, 5, 7 or 9 is prime

quiz.q: Why is 21 NOT a prime number?
options: It can be arranged as 3 rows of 7
quiz.explain: 21 = 3 × 7, so it has more than two factors.
quiz.mistake: Gives a reason that does not use factors

quiz.q: How many factors does a prime number have?
quiz.explain: Exactly two: 1 and itself.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a prime has one factor

quiz.q: Is 1 a prime number?
options: Yes, because it is the smallest
No, it has only one factor
quiz.explain: A prime needs exactly two different factors. 1 has only one.

quiz.q: Which number makes the most arrays?
quiz.mistake: Picks the biggest number without checking

teach.ask: Gappu has 17 seeds and wants to put them in a rectangle with more than one row. Can I? Why?
teach.praise: 17 is prime! Its only factors are 1 and 17, so only one row works.

topics.title: Skip jumps on the number line

learn.hook: A frog jumps 3 steps at a time from 0. Will it ever land on 20? Let's hop along and see!
points: An animal that jumps the same size each time makes a skip pattern.
Jumping 3 at a time from 0 lands on 3, 6, 9, 12, … These are multiples of 3.
Landing spot = number of jumps × jump size. 6 jumps of 4 land on 24.
Starting at 2 and jumping 5 gives 2, 7, 12, 17, … (add 5 each time).
Jumping backwards means subtracting the jump size each time.

example.q: A frog jumps 4 steps at a time, starting at 0. Where is it after 6 jumps?

learn.reallife: Skip counting helps us count money in ₹5 or ₹10 notes and count pairs of socks quickly.

games.title: True or false?
items: Jumps of 2 from 0 land only on even numbers.
2, 4, 6, 8, … are all even.
Jumps of 5 from 0 can land on 34.
Jumps of 5 from 0 land only on numbers ending in 0 or 5.
Jumps of 10 from 0 always land on numbers ending in 0.
Jumps of 3 from 0 land on 20.
They land on 18 and then 21, skipping 20.
A frog jumping 4 at a time from 0 lands on 100.

quiz.q: A rabbit jumps 5 steps at a time from 0. Where is it after 4 jumps?
quiz.explain: 4 jumps × 5 = 20.

quiz.q: A frog jumps 3 steps at a time from 0. Which spot will it land on?
quiz.explain: 15 = 3 × 5, so the frog lands on 15. 10, 14 and 20 are not multiples of 3.
quiz.mistake: Picks a number that is near a landing spot

quiz.q: A grasshopper jumps 4 steps at a time from 0. How many jumps does it take to reach 28?
quiz.explain: 28 ÷ 4 = 7 jumps.

quiz.q: A kangaroo starts at 2 and jumps 5 each time: 2, 7, 12, 17, … Where does it land next?
quiz.mistake: Thinks it must land on multiples of 5, forgetting it started at 2

quiz.q: A squirrel starts at 30 and jumps back 6 each time. Where is it after 3 jumps?
A frog jumps 7 steps at a time from 0. Will it land on 50?
options: No, 50 is not a multiple of 7
quiz.explain: 7 × 7 = 49 and 7 × 8 = 56. The frog jumps over 50.

quiz.q: A deer leaps 6 steps at a time from 0. Where does it land on its 10th leap?
A frog starts at 1 and jumps 3 each time: 1, 4, 7, 10, 13, … Which of these will it land on?
quiz.explain: 13 + 3 = 16. 18, 20 and 21 are not in this pattern.
quiz.mistake: Picks a multiple of 3 (18 or 21), forgetting the frog started at 1

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'A frog jumps 4 at a time from 0. How do I know where it lands after 6 jumps?'
teach.praise: Ribbit! 6 jumps of 4 is 6 × 4 = 24. Multiply the jumps by the jump size!
teach.nudge: How big is each jump? How do I use the number of jumps?

learn.hook: A frog jumps 2 at a time and a rabbit jumps 3 at a time. Where will they land on the same spot? Let's race them!
points: A common multiple of two numbers is a multiple of both. 12 is a common multiple of 3 and 4.
Two animals starting at 0 land together on the common multiples of their jump sizes.
The first spot where they meet (after 0) is the smallest common multiple.
To find common multiples, list the multiples of each number and look for the numbers in both lists.

example.q: A frog jumps 3 at a time and a rabbit jumps 4 at a time, both from 0. Where do they first land on the same spot?

learn.reallife: If two friends visit the park every 2 and 3 days, common multiples tell when they meet.

quiz.q: A frog jumps 2 and a rabbit jumps 3, both from 0. Where do they first land on the same spot?
quiz.explain: Frog: 2, 4, 6. Rabbit: 3, 6. They first meet at 6.

quiz.q: Which of these is a common multiple of 4 and 6?
quiz.explain: 12 is in both lists: 4 × 3 = 12 and 6 × 2 = 12. 16 is only a multiple of 4; 18 only of 6.
quiz.mistake: Picks a number that is a multiple of only one of them

quiz.q: What is the smallest common multiple of 5 and 10?
quiz.explain: 10 is a multiple of 5 (5 × 2) and of 10 (10 × 1).

quiz.q: A frog jumps 4 and a rabbit jumps 6, both from 0. On a number line from 0 to 30, on how many spots (not counting 0) do both land?
quiz.explain: Common multiples of 4 and 6 up to 30 are 12 and 24. That is 2 spots.
quiz.mistake: Counts 0 as a landing spot, or misses 24

quiz.q: Which number is a common multiple of 3 and 5?
quiz.explain: 15 = 3 × 5. It is in both times tables. 20 and 25 are only multiples of 5; 18 only of 3.
quiz.mistake: Picks a multiple of just one number

quiz.q: Which list shows all the common multiples of 2 and 5 that are less than 40?
quiz.explain: A number that is a multiple of both 2 and 5 ends in 0: 10, 20, 30.

quiz.q: A rabbit jumps 3 at a time and a kangaroo jumps 9 at a time, both from 0. Where do they first meet?
quiz.explain: 9 is a multiple of 3 (3 × 3), so they first meet at 9.
quiz.mistake: Always multiplies the jump sizes (27) or adds them (12)

quiz.q: Is 20 a common multiple of 4 and 6?
options: No, 20 is not a multiple of 6
No, 20 is not a multiple of 4
quiz.explain: 20 = 4 × 5, but 6 × 3 = 18 and 6 × 4 = 24, so 20 is not a multiple of 6.
quiz.mistake: Checks only one of the two numbers

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'What is a common multiple? Where will two jumping animals meet?'
teach.praise: Yippee! A common multiple is in both times tables. The first one is where they first meet!
teach.nudge: Must the number be in one list or both lists? Which one is the first meeting spot?

learn.hook: A frog jumps 4 and a rabbit jumps 6. Both want to reach the carrot at 30. Who can land on it?
points: List multiples of each jump size to find where each animal lands.
Common multiples of 4 and 6: 12, 24, 36, 48, 60 … They go up by 12 each time.
Pattern: every common multiple is a multiple of the smallest one.
An animal lands on a target only if the target is a multiple of its jump size: the rabbit lands on 30 (6 × 5), the frog does not.
To see who gets there in fewer jumps, divide the target by each jump size.

example.q: List five common multiples of 3 and 4.

learn.reallife: Two buses on routes that repeat every 4 and 6 minutes meet at the depot every 12 minutes.

games.title: Lands on 30?
items: Jumps of 6
Jumps of 5
Jumps of 3
Jumps of 10
Jumps of 4
Jumps of 7
Jumps of 8
Jumps of 9

quiz.q: Which list shows the first five common multiples of 4 and 6?
quiz.explain: They are multiples of 12, the smallest common multiple.
quiz.mistake: Includes numbers that are multiples of only one

quiz.q: What pattern do the common multiples of 3 and 4 show?
options: They go up by 12 each time
They go up by 7 each time
They go up by 3 each time
quiz.explain: 12, 24, 36 … each is 12 more.

quiz.q: A frog jumps 4 and a rabbit jumps 6 from 0. Who lands exactly on 30?
quiz.explain: 30 = 6 × 5, so the rabbit lands there. 30 ÷ 4 leaves a remainder, so the frog does not.
quiz.mistake: Thinks bigger jumps miss more spots

quiz.q: Both animals (jumps of 4 and 6) want to reach 24. How many jumps does the rabbit need?
quiz.explain: 24 ÷ 6 = 4 jumps.

quiz.q: How many jumps does the frog (jumps of 4) need to reach 24?
quiz.explain: 24 ÷ 4 = 6 jumps.

quiz.q: A deer jumps 5 and a hare jumps 3 from 0. Which spot do they both land on?
quiz.explain: 45 is a multiple of both 5 and 3.
quiz.mistake: Picks a multiple of only one

quiz.q: Which number is NOT a common multiple of 2 and 5?
quiz.explain: 25 is not even, so it is not a multiple of 2.

quiz.q: How many common multiples of 4 and 6 are there from 1 to 50?
quiz.explain: 12, 24, 36 and 48: four of them.

teach.ask: Gappu jumps 3 and his friend jumps 5. Will we both land on 20? On 30?
teach.praise: We both land on 30 because it is a multiple of 3 and 5, but only my friend lands on 20!

learn.hook: Two temple bells ring every 4 and 6 minutes. They ring together at 7:00. When will they ring together again?
points: When two things repeat at different gaps, they happen together at common multiples of the gaps.
The next time they happen together is the smallest common multiple.
If one number is a multiple of the other, the bigger number is the smallest common multiple: for 4 and 8 it is 8.
List multiples of the bigger number and check which is also a multiple of the smaller one. That is quick!

example.q: Bell A rings every 4 minutes and bell B every 6 minutes. Both ring at 7:00 a.m. When do they next ring together?
steps: Is 6 a multiple of 4? No. Is 12? Yes

learn.reallife: Bus timings, festival lights blinking at different speeds and buying packs to get equal numbers all use common multiples.

games.title: True or false?
items: The smallest common multiple of 4 and 8 is 32.
8 is already a multiple of 4, so the answer is 8.
Two numbers have many common multiples.
For 2 and 3: 6, 12, 18, 24, … they go on forever.
Every common multiple of 2 and 3 is also a multiple of 6.
6, 12, 18, … are all multiples of 6.
Multiplying two numbers always gives their smallest common multiple.
For 6 and 9, 6 × 9 = 54, but 18 is smaller and works.
24 is a common multiple of 6 and 8.

quiz.q: Two bells ring every 6 minutes and every 8 minutes. They ring together at 9:00 a.m. After how many minutes do they ring together again?
quiz.explain: Multiples of 8: 8, 16, 24. 24 is also a multiple of 6. So after 24 minutes.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies 6 × 8 (48), which is a common multiple but not the first

quiz.q: Riya visits the library every 4 days and Kabir every 6 days. They were both there today. In how many days will they meet there again?
quiz.explain: Multiples of 6: 6, 12. 12 is also a multiple of 4. They meet in 12 days.

quiz.q: Laddoos come in boxes of 6 and pedas in boxes of 4. Meena wants the same number of each. What is the smallest number she can buy of each?
quiz.explain: 12 is the smallest number in both the 6 and 4 times tables. 2 boxes of laddoos and 3 boxes of pedas.

quiz.q: Two strings of Diwali lights blink every 3 seconds and every 5 seconds. They blink together now. After how many seconds will they blink together again?
quiz.explain: 3 and 5 have no common multiple smaller than 15. 15 = 3 × 5.

quiz.q: A blue bus leaves the depot every 10 minutes and a red bus every 15 minutes. Both leave at 8:00 a.m. When do they next leave together?
quiz.explain: Multiples of 15: 15, 30. 30 is a multiple of 10. 8:00 + 30 minutes = 8:30 a.m.

quiz.q: Arjun waters plant A every 2 days and plant B every 5 days. He waters both today. How many days until he waters both on the same day again?
quiz.explain: Multiples of 5: 5, 10. 10 is a multiple of 2. So 10 days.

quiz.q: What is the smallest common multiple of 4 and 8?
quiz.explain: 8 is a multiple of 4 (4 × 2), so 8 is the smallest common multiple.

quiz.q: Aisha's cricket club meets every 3 days and her dance class every 9 days. Both are on Monday. After how many days are both on the same day again?
quiz.explain: 9 is a multiple of 3, so after 9 days.

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'Two bells ring every 4 and every 6 minutes. How do I know when they ring together again?'
teach.praise: Ding dong! The first common multiple of 4 and 6 is 12. They ring together after 12 minutes!
teach.nudge: What should I list for each bell? Which number do I look for?

learn.hook: Which jump sizes from 0 land on both 24 and 36? Those are their common factors!
points: A common factor of two numbers divides both of them exactly.
A jump size that lands on both 24 and 36 (starting at 0) is a common factor.
To find all common factors, list the factors of each number and pick the ones in both lists.
Some pairs like 12 and 13 have only 1 as a common factor.

example.q: Find the common factors of 18 and 24.

learn.reallife: Packing 24 laddoos and 36 barfis into the same number of equal boxes uses common factors.

items.text: Biggest common factor of 24 and 36 is ___

quiz.q: Which jump size from 0 lands on both 24 and 36?
quiz.explain: 6 divides 24 (4 jumps) and 36 (6 jumps).
quiz.mistake: Picks a factor of only one number

quiz.q: Which list shows all the common factors of 24 and 36?
quiz.explain: These are in both factor lists. 8 is not a factor of 36.

quiz.q: What is the only common factor of 12 and 13?
quiz.explain: 13 is prime, and 13 does not divide 12. So only 1 is common.
quiz.mistake: Thinks there must be a bigger one

quiz.q: Which is a common factor of 15 and 25?
quiz.explain: 5 divides both 15 and 25.

quiz.q: How many common factors do 16 and 24 have?
What is the biggest common factor of 18 and 27?
quiz.explain: Factors of 18: 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18. Of 27: 1, 3, 9, 27. Biggest common: 9.

quiz.q: Which pair has only 1 as a common factor?
quiz.explain: 8 = 2 × 2 × 2 and 9 = 3 × 3 share nothing but 1.
quiz.mistake: Thinks odd and even numbers always share a factor

quiz.q: 24 laddoos and 36 barfis go into equal boxes, each box with only one kind and the same number in each. What is the most sweets per box?
quiz.explain: The number per box must divide both 24 and 36. The biggest is 12.
quiz.mistake: Uses a factor of just one number

teach.ask: Gappu wants to know the common factors of 10 and 20. How do I find them?
teach.praise: Factors of 10 are 1, 2, 5, 10, and all of them divide 20. So 1, 2, 5, 10!
teach.nudge: Which numbers divide both 10 and 20 exactly?

topics.title: Patterns in common factors and choosing jumps

learn.hook: Find common factors of 8 and 9, 14 and 15, 20 and 21… do you notice something?
points: Two consecutive numbers (like 14 and 15) always have only 1 as a common factor.
If one number divides the other (like 6 and 18), the common factors are just the factors of the smaller number.
Two even numbers always have 2 as a common factor.
To reach one number but skip another, choose a jump size that is a factor of the first but not of the second.
Example: to land on 20 but not on 15, jump 2, 4, 10 or 20.

example.q: Which jump sizes land on 12 but skip 18?

learn.reallife: A watchman who checks every 4th house will visit house 12 but walk past house 18!

games.title: Spot the pattern
items: Two consecutive numbers have only 1 as a common factor.
Like 20 and 21.
The common factors of 6 and 18 are the factors of 6.
6 divides 18.
Two even numbers always have 2 as a common factor.
Both divide by 2.
Two odd numbers always have only 1 as a common factor.
9 and 15 share 3.
A jump of 5 lands on 20 but not on 15.
5 lands on both.

quiz.q: What are the common factors of 20 and 21?
quiz.explain: 20 and 21 are consecutive numbers, so only 1 divides both.
quiz.mistake: Finds a factor of only one number

quiz.q: What are the common factors of 6 and 18?
quiz.explain: 6 divides 18, so every factor of 6 divides 18 too.
quiz.mistake: Lists factors of the bigger number

quiz.q: Which number is a common factor of ANY two even numbers?
quiz.explain: Every even number divides by 2.

quiz.q: Which pair of odd numbers has a common factor other than 1?
quiz.explain: 9 and 15 both divide by 3.
quiz.mistake: Thinks odd numbers never share factors

quiz.q: Which jump size lands on 12 but NOT on 18?
quiz.explain: 4 divides 12 but not 18. 2, 3 and 6 divide both.

quiz.q: Which jump size lands on 20 but not on 15?
quiz.explain: 10 divides 20 but not 15.

quiz.q: Which jump size lands on 15 but not on 20?
quiz.explain: 3 divides 15 but not 20.

quiz.q: Which is true for every pair of consecutive numbers?
quiz.explain: Any number dividing both would also divide their difference, 1. So only 1 works.

teach.ask: Gappu wants a jump size that lands on 16 but never on 24. Which jumps can I use?
teach.praise: Factors of 16 are 1, 2, 4, 8, 16. Only 16 does not divide 24, so I must jump 16!
teach.nudge: Which factors of 16 are not factors of 24?

learn.hook: Without dividing, can you tell whether 3,470 can be shared equally into 10 groups? Just look at the last digit!
points: A number is divisible by 2 if its ones digit is even: 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8.
A number is divisible by 5 if it ends in 0 or 5.
A number is divisible by 10 if it ends in 0.
A number ending in 0 is divisible by 2, 5 and 10 — all three!
Sort numbers by checking the ones digit only.

steps: Does not end in 0 → not by 10

learn.reallife: Shopkeepers know a price ending in 0 can be paid exactly with ₹10 notes!

games.title: Divisibility facts
items: A number ending in 0 is divisible by 10.
Like 70 or 1,230.
Every number divisible by 5 is divisible by 10.
35 is divisible by 5 but not by 10.
Every number divisible by 10 is divisible by 2.
It ends in 0, which is even.
4,682 is divisible by 2.
It ends in 2.
1,005 is divisible by 2.
It ends in 5, an odd digit.

quiz.q: Which number is divisible by 2?
quiz.explain: It ends in 8, an even digit.

quiz.q: Which number is divisible by 5?
quiz.explain: It ends in 5.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any odd number divides by 5

quiz.q: Which number is divisible by 10?
quiz.explain: It ends in 0.
quiz.mistake: Picks a number with a 0 somewhere inside

quiz.q: Is 3,475 divisible by 10?
options: No, it does not end in 0
quiz.explain: Only numbers ending in 0 are divisible by 10.

quiz.q: Which number is divisible by 2, 5 and 10?
quiz.explain: 560 ends in 0, so it is divisible by all three.
quiz.mistake: Checks only one of the rules

quiz.q: Which number is divisible by 5 but NOT by 2?
quiz.explain: 85 ends in 5: divisible by 5 but odd.

quiz.q: Which number is divisible by 2 but NOT by 5?
quiz.explain: 124 is even but does not end in 0 or 5.

quiz.q: How many of these are divisible by 10: 40, 45, 100, 305, 990?
quiz.explain: 40, 100 and 990 end in 0.

teach.ask: Gappu found 1,250 seeds. Can I share them equally into 2 piles? 5 piles? 10 piles?
teach.praise: 1,250 ends in 0, so it can be shared into 2, 5 or 10 equal piles!
teach.nudge: What is the ones digit of 1,250?

topics.title: True or false: factors and multiples

learn.hook: '0 is a factor of 10.' True or false? Let us test tricky statements like a maths detective!
points: 0 is not a factor of any number, because we cannot divide by 0 (0 × anything = 0, never 10).
Every number is a multiple of 1, and 1 is a factor of every number.
The sum of two consecutive numbers is always odd.
Multiples of 8 are always multiples of 4, but multiples of 4 are not always multiples of 8 (12).
To show a statement is false, one counterexample is enough.

example.q: Is 'every multiple of 4 is a multiple of 8' true?
steps: 12 ÷ 8 leaves 4, so 12 is not a multiple of 8
One counterexample shows it is false

learn.reallife: Detectives look for one clue that breaks a story. In maths, one counterexample breaks a false claim!

games.title: Decide
items: 0 is a factor of 10.
0 × anything is 0, never 10.
Every number is a multiple of 1.
Any number = 1 × itself.
The sum of two consecutive numbers is always odd.
One is odd, one is even.
Every multiple of 4 is a multiple of 8.
12 is a multiple of 4 but not 8.
Every multiple of 8 is a multiple of 4.
A prime number has exactly two factors.
1 and itself.

games.title: Counterexample
pairs: All multiples of 4 are multiples of 8
All even numbers are multiples of 4

quiz.q: Is 0 a factor of 10?
options: Yes, 0 is a factor of every number
quiz.explain: A factor times some number must give 10. 0 times anything is 0.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 0 is a factor of every number

quiz.q: Which statement about 0 and 1 is true?
options: Every even number is a multiple of 4
1 is a factor of every number
0 is a factor of every number
Every number is a multiple of 0
quiz.explain: Any number ÷ 1 leaves no remainder.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the roles of 0 and 1

quiz.q: 'The sum of two consecutive numbers is always odd.' True or false?
quiz.explain: One of them is odd and one is even, and odd + even = odd: 7 + 8 = 15.
quiz.mistake: Tests only one example and doubts it

quiz.q: Which number shows that 'every multiple of 4 is a multiple of 8' is false?
quiz.explain: 12 is a multiple of 4 but 12 ÷ 8 leaves 4.
quiz.mistake: Picks a number that agrees with the claim

quiz.q: 'Every multiple of 6 is a multiple of 3.' True or false?
quiz.mistake: Thinks the claim works only one way

quiz.q: Which is a counterexample to 'all odd numbers are prime'?
quiz.explain: 9 is odd but 9 = 3 × 3, so it is not prime.

quiz.q: 'The product of two consecutive numbers is always even.' True or false?
quiz.explain: One of them is even, and any number times an even number is even: 4 × 5 = 20.

quiz.q: Which statement is false?
options: Every factor of 24 is a factor of 12
Every factor of 12 is a factor of 24
Every multiple of 24 is a multiple of 12
quiz.explain: 8 is a factor of 24 but not of 12, so that statement is false.

teach.ask: Gappu says 'all even numbers are multiples of 4'. Is he right? Can you find a counterexample?
teach.praise: 6 is even but not a multiple of 4. So I was wrong!
teach.nudge: Can you find an even number that 4 does not divide?
